what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It contains two different medicines working together: trandolapril (an ACE inhibitor) helps relax your blood vessels, and verapamil (a calcium channel blocker) helps slow your heart rate and further relax blood vessels. Together, they help lower your blood pressure and reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Taking it with food helps your body absorb it properly and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood pressure, other health conditions, and other medicines you take. The usual starting dose is one tablet once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose over time. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking this medicine — it can increase the amount of verapamil in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and cause dizziness. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine may cause dizziness, especially at first. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); severe dizziness or fainting; chest pain or a very slow or irregular heartbeat; shortness of breath or difficulty breathing; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or an irregular heartbeat; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Also contact your doctor if you develop a dry, persistent cough that does not go away, as this is a common side effect of the trandolapril part of this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to see some lowering of your blood pressure within the first few days of taking this medicine, but it may take 2 to 4 weeks to get the full benefit. Keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel well. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so it is important not to stop just because you feel fine. Your doctor will check your blood pressure regularly to make sure the medicine is working.
special_populations: Pregnant women: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Both medicines in this tablet can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially in the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as verapamil passes into breast milk and the effects are not fully known. Older adults: You may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure. Use caution when standing up. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
